facts.statement: Officer of the Bengal Medical Service; participant in the Second Anglo-Afghan War.
Recollections of the Kabul Campaign, 1879 & 1880 published 1883.
Life dates 1847–1920; Bengal Medical Service 1868–1902 and 1914–17; retired as lieutenant-colonel in 1902.

en.intro: Duke writes from the moving army’s daily world: camps, marches, illness and the effort to keep men fit for service. The campaign becomes visible through the concerns of a medical officer.
en.orientation: His account belongs to the Second Anglo-Afghan War of 1878–80. It describes the renewed fighting around Kabul after the destruction of the British residency in 1879.
career: Service in the Bengal Medical Service placed him within the British Indian military establishment. His recollections follow operations in which he took part, rather than assembling a later general history.
literature: Published in 1883, the book preserves a participant’s sequence of movement and observation. The medical standpoint gives particular weight to physical endurance and the conditions of campaigning.
en.legacy: Duke widens the field of military remembrance. Battles depend on bodies, transport and care as well as on orders.
en.bridge: The edition brings forward the daily material of the Kabul campaign, recorded by a serving medical officer.
